From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook, compared against the Seller's untrusted draft

## Preliminary warning: how the Seller has framed the package

Before the issue-by-issue review, the team should know how the Seller has framed this draft.

- **"[STANDARD]" labels.** The Seller has tagged almost every contentious clause "[STANDARD]". Its "Reviewer Efficiency Note" asks us to review only "[OPEN]" items. **Nothing in the package is actually marked [OPEN].** Following the note would mean reviewing nothing. I have ignored the labels and reviewed every clause on its merits.
- **"Settled at principal level" / "FINAL".** The Seller says the positions were agreed by both deal teams. Under our playbook, the 20% cap and 18-month period need **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft**. None has been given. The Seller's statement is not that authority. Please do not treat anything here as agreed without confirming with Amelia directly.
- **"Market context" preamble.** These are the Seller's assertions about market norms, not neutral benchmarks. They do not change our positions.
- **Seller's own Disclosure Letter.** It contradicts the Seller's comfort statements. It confirms there is no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, and bonuses missing from the funds flow. It also states that the incident is unresolved.

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% fallback is usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The fallback is not unlocked: no written authority exists, and the Seller's "principal-level" claim is not a substitute.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket. Only the excess over the basket is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 5,000 de minimis. AUD 50,000 basket. Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket.** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours and the deductible structure permanently removes the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13). Also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion. 18 months requires Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** The fallback is not authorised, and the default wording would silently pull Fundamental, Fraud and Indemnity claims into the 18-month bar.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap (AUD 24,000,000);
  - a period of at least six years;
  - exclusion from the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for, so capping them at 20% for 18 months is not an administrative point.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
  - caps;
  - baskets;
  - time limits;
  - exclusive remedy;
  - non-reliance.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright. Insert a full fraud carve-out. This is non-negotiable.** The playbook says no one may waive this, and "all Claims of any nature" would purport to cap the Seller's own fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 22 Sept 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2). The Seller says the framework is "already accepted".
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DL 1.1–1.2. Accept only specific disclosures (DL 2–10), subject to a fair-disclosure standard.** We have not accepted the framework, and blanket disclosure would gut the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause. If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - rely on named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry;
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** Combined with data-room disclosure, it would bar claims for the very issues our due diligence found, including indemnified ones.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Completion condition. Reasonable endeavours is not enough.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective Bluefen consent, with evidence the conditions are satisfied, a condition precedent.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m), and DL 2 confirms neither the consent nor evidence of its conditions exists.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release of the approximately AUD 3,200,000 facility "to be provided following Completion".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - effective security releases at Completion.
  A post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require a payout letter, repayment from the funds flow, and executed discharges delivered at Completion.** DL 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and undischarged, and we have neither the undertaking nor Amelia's approval for a post-Completion release.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 in DD-005 bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) shown as a specific funds-flow line item or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Add a funds-flow line item (or Debt/Seller-funded treatment) covering bonuses and on-costs, with an indemnity.** DL 5 confirms they are omitted and on-costs are unaddressed, so the cost would otherwise land on the Company after we own it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a broadened indemnity covering IP ownership and infringement losses connected to Ironquay;
  - preservation of the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the narrow form. Broaden the indemnity and require evidence of payment or a confirmatory assignment.** The AUD 180,000 is unverified either way (DL 4), and the real exposure is the IP itself, not just the fee.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - log preservation;
  - completion of the investigation;
  - updates before Completion;
  - appropriate warranty or indemnity protection.
  We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss amount in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation. Add pre-Completion covenants on preservation, investigation and updates, and keep the matter outside the general disclosure bar.** DL 6 itself says access, scope and notification duties are unresolved, so "not material" is unsupported. We should equally not overstate it.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000, described as ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold. Do not accept "ordinary course" and do not claim a deduction yet; request information and reserve treatment.** DL 8 admits these points are unstated, so the right classification needs facts first.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature". Tax and IP are folded into the general regime. Title is under general caps.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as separate categories, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Draft express carve-outs so each category has its own regime and the general limitations do not override them.** The "all Claims" drafting is a single override that collapses every protection into the 20% / 18-month box.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the company share register (DD-012).
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as:
  - ASIC searches;
  - a PPSR search;
  - original share certificates;
  - board and shareholder authorities.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone. Require independent verification as a Completion deliverable.** DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal record, and DL 10 concedes we have not verified it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain OPEN. We assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation. Record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** No agreement has been reached, and the playbook does not presume any outcome.

## Summary and next steps

1. **Every substantive Seller position falls short of the playbook.** None should be accepted as drafted. SPA-N-013 is the only "hold pending facts" item.
2. **Non-negotiables:** the fraud carve-out (005), the Fundamental regime (004), and deletion of the "all Claims" overrides (003, 014).
3. **Fallbacks are locked.** Neither the 20% cap nor 18 months is available without Amelia Frost's written, draft-specific authority. Please confirm with her directly rather than relying on the Seller's statement that positions were "settled at principal level".
4. **Cover note to the Seller:** we suggest the mark-up states expressly that the Buyer does not accept the "[STANDARD]" categorisation, the "FINAL" designation, or the claim that the disclosure and limitation framework has been accepted.

I can prepare the clause-level mark-up or the cover note if helpful.
